Actions/Abilities/Ability---All-the-Bird.title: Ability - All the Birds
Actions/Abilities/Ability---All-the-Bird.content:
AP Cost: +4
Make a melee strike against all targets in a skirmish. Resolve strikes one after another. Roll Attack and Damage once.
Tags:StrikeAoE

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Anatomical-K.title: Ability - Anatomical Knowledge
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Anatomical-K.content:
AP Cost: 1
Roll [Deduce] against enemy using Biology or Medicine. On success you learn enemy’s weaknesses and resistances.

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Arcane-Mind.title: Ability - Arcane Mind
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Arcane-Mind.content:
AP Cost: R
Before rolling against aMind spell, add +2 Competence bonus to your Endure roll.
Tags:ReactionEndure

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Behind-the-S.title: Ability - Behind the Shield Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Behind-the-S.content:
AP Cost: +1
Strike from behind the shield. Enemy takes -2 to Deflect against this attack.
Tags:Strike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Bowling-Stri.title: Ability - Bowling Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Bowling-Stri.content:
AP Cost: +3
As Home Run, but you may aim the launched enemy at another creature along the flight path. The second target defends against your attack roll as aProjectile (Dodge, or Deflect where allowed) — their friend counts as the projectile. On a failed defense, the second target takes your weapon damage and both end up in the same skirmish. (Damage split/Prone riders TBD at playtest.)
Tags:StrikeProjectileMovement

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Calf-Strike.title: Ability - Calf Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Calf-Strike.content:
AP Cost: 2
Strike the blunt end of your weapon at enemy’s calf. If you hit, the enemy rolls Endurance against your Might. On a failure, they halve their speed until the end of their turn.
Tags:Strike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Chokehold.title: Ability - Chokehold
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Chokehold.content:
AP Cost: 1
Requirement: You are grappling the target.
Lock the grabbed target’s throat. Until the start of your next turn, the target cannot speak or cast spells that require voice.
Tags:BrawlingBane

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Come-and-Get.title: Ability - Come and Get Me
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Come-and-Get.content:
AP Cost: 2
Make a Feint check against an enemy in your skirmish.
On success, you reposition and they are pulled along with you — neither of you spends a Reaction:

If you were in a duel (a skirmish of two), you both enter another skirmish in your zone — goading them into your friends.
If you were in a larger skirmish, you both leave it and form a duel — goading them away from theirs.

On failure, you simply Disengage and Engage as normal.
This is combat flowing through the zone — the fight moves because you make it move.
Tags:MovementMind

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Counter-Grab.title: Ability - Counter Grab
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Counter-Grab.content:
AP Cost: R
Trigger: You critically succeed a Deflect against a melee attack.
Effect: Immediately attempt a Grapple on the attacker without spending AP. Failure does not grant a free attack.
Tags:ReactionBrawling

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Dodge-Roll.title: Ability - Dodge-Roll
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Dodge-Roll.content:
AP Cost: R
Trigger: You are targeted by aBurst or AoE effect.
While Unencumbered, add +3 to your Dodge against the effect. On success, move up to half your Speed.
Tags:ReactionDodgeMovement

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Double-Shot.title: Ability - Double Shot
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Double-Shot.content:
AP Cost: 4
Shoot two different targets, second at -2 to hit.
Tags:AttackProjectile

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Double-Strik.title: Ability - Double Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Double-Strik.content:
AP Cost: 0 (modifier)
Strike with both weapons for -2 AP total cost. If the enemy successfully defends against the first strike, the second misses automatically.
Tags:Strike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Drive-into-F.title: Ability - Drive into Fervor
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Drive-into-F.content:
AP Cost: 2
Your team are your loyal followers who have sworn an oath to you. Drive them into fervor for 1 turn.

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Follow-Up-St.title: Ability - Follow-Up Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Follow-Up-St.content:
AP Cost: -1
Requirnment: Your previous strike was a hit.
Make a basic strike with -1 AP cost.
Tags:Strike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Guardian-Aur.title: Ability - Guardian Aura
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Guardian-Aur.content:
AP Cost: R
All allies in your zone are protected by your aura. You can provide advantage to your allies as a reaction on any defense. When used against AOE, you provide it to all affected allies.
Tags:ReactionAuralimit1

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Hair-Trigger.title: Ability - Hair Trigger
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Hair-Trigger.content:
AP Cost: Variable (readied action)
Ready a ranged strike with a trigger of “target enters my line of sight” or “target enters my zone or a zone within my weapon’s range,” or both.
When any hostile target qualifies, make the attack without spending a Reaction. Once per round.
Tags:RangedStrike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Herding-Stri.title: Ability - Herding Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Herding-Stri.content:
AP Cost: +2
Declare when making a strike with an Impact or Unarmed weapon. On a hit, deal damage normally; the target rolls Endure vs your attack roll, with a bonus equal to the number of their allies in their skirmish (up to +3). On a failure, they are forcefully disengaged and engaged into a skirmish of your choice in the zone.
Tags:StrikeMovement

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Home-Run.title: Ability - Home Run
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Home-Run.content:
AP Cost: +3
Declare when making a strike with an Impact or Unarmed weapon. On a hit, the target rolls Endure vs your attack roll, with a bonus equal to the number of their allies in their skirmish (up to +3). On a failure they are launched: moved along lines toward a zone of your choice, up to half your attack roll in distance (playtest: maybe the full roll), or into a wall or obstacle if one is closer. If the flight is not stopped one way or another, the attack deals critical damage.
Tags:StrikeMovement

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Inspirer.title: Ability - Inspirer
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Inspirer.content:
AP Cost: R
After succeeding a non-hostile check, you can spend a reaction to give your allies a +2 morale bonus for the same action until the start of your next turn. Bonus applies only to the next attempt, not ongoing effects. GM determines when checks are similar enough for the bonus to apply.
Tags:Reaction

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Just-the-Two.title: Ability - Just the Two of Us
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Just-the-Two.content:
AP Cost: 2
While in a duel (a skirmish of just you and one enemy), proclaim it a duel led by destiny. Until the duel ends, anyone attempting to interfere — engaging the duel or acting into it — must roll Resolve vs your Manipulation + CH. On a failure they cannot Engage the duel this turn and take -2 on checks made into it.
Tags:Mind

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Mighty-Charg.title: Ability - Mighty Charge
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Mighty-Charg.content:
AP Cost: 2 + Weapon Strike
Sprint in a straight line into the target’s zone and make a strike, engaging as part of the attack. The strike deals extra damage equal to half the Cost of the lines you crossed during the charge (rounded down). Movement is paid separately as a normal Move.
Tags:StrikeMovement

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Mobile-Draw.title: Ability - Mobile Draw
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Mobile-Draw.content:
AP Cost: -
#Move
Declare a ranged attack.  Move to an adjacent zone for number of AP your attack has. At the end of the movement make an attack.
Tags:RangedMovementMove

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Monkey-King-.title: Ability - Monkey King Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Monkey-King-.content:
AP Cost: +2
Disengage, engage a different skirmish attacking up to 3 targets.
Tags:StrikeAoE

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Overswing.title: Ability - Overswing
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Overswing.content:
AP Cost: R
When attacking with an axe and the defender declares a Deflect before the roll, you can spend your reaction to gain +2 Situational bonus to hit and -2 to all Deflect checks until the start of your next turn.
Tags:ReactionStrike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Painful-Parr.title: Ability - Painful Parry
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Painful-Parr.content:
AP Cost: R
When critically succeeding deflecting against a melee attack, make a free light weapon strike as a reaction.
Tags:ReactionDeflectStrike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Piranha-Stri.title: Ability - Piranha Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Piranha-Stri.content:
When striking an off-guard target with a Light weapon, you may take a penalty to your attack roll to increase your weapon damage die.





















PenaltyDamage Die Increase-1d4→d6, d6→d8, d8→d10, d10→d12-2d4→d8, d6→d10, d8→d12-3d4→d10, d6→d12
Tags:AttackStrikeMelee

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Predictive-D.title: Ability - Predictive Defense
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Predictive-D.content:
AP Cost: 1
Preroll your next Deflect or Dodge defense. After seeing the attacker’s roll, choose whether to use this prediction or roll normally.
Unused predictions fade at end of your turn.
Tags:MentalDeflectDodge

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Predictive-S.title: Ability - Predictive Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Predictive-S.content:
AP Cost: 1
Preroll your next attack using Wit instead of your weapon’s normal attribute. When you make the attack, choose whether to use this prediction or roll normally.
Unused predictions fade at end of your turn.
Tags:MentalStrike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Reactive-Pre.title: Ability - Reactive Prediction
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Reactive-Pre.content:
AP Cost: R
When rolling Dodge or Deflect, spend a Reaction to roll with Advantage.
Tags:ReactionDefenseMental

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Reactive-Str.title: Ability - Reactive Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Reactive-Str.content:
AP Cost: R
When an enemy attempts to leave the skirmish without disengaging first, make a free strike as a reaction before they leave their space.
Tags:ReactionStrike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Ricochet-Sho.title: Ability - Ricochet Shot
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Ricochet-Sho.content:
AP Cost: TBD
Bounce an arrow off a hard surface to strike a target behind cover or around a corner. The target does not benefit from cover or barrier line-effects against this attack.
Tags:AttackProjectile

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Riposte.title: Ability - Riposte
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Riposte.content:
AP Cost: R
When an enemy critically fails on their attack or you critically succeed defending against it, make a strike against the enemy as a reaction.
Tags:ReactionStrike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Rocket-Strik.title: Ability - Rocket Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Rocket-Strik.content:
WIP — the absurd apex of the shove line.
AP Cost: +3
As Home Run, but the launch is skyward: the target is removed from the map, flying up for a round, and falls at the end of their next turn — taking falling damage and landing Prone in the zone they left (or where the GM rules). If they cannot fly or otherwise arrest the fall, they are effectively out of the fight for a round.
Tags:StrikeMovement

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Shield-Block.title: Ability - Shield Block
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Shield-Block.content:
AP Cost: R
Trigger: You fail at a Deflect with a Shield, but haven’t applied damage yet.
Effect: Reduce the damage by Shield Negation.
Tags:DeflectBlock

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Shield-Guard.title: Ability - Shield Guardian
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Shield-Guard.content:
AP Cost: R
Trigger: An ally in your skirmish is attacked.
Effect: Use your reaction to attempt deflect instead of them. If this is an AOE effect, you protect both of you.
Tags:ReactionBlock

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Shield-Rush.title: Ability - Shield Rush
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Shield-Rush.content:
AP Cost: 4
Move twice and strike with your shield, adding Might to the damage twice.
Tags:StrikeMovement

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Shield-Warde.title: Ability - Shield Warden
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Shield-Warde.content:
AP Cost: R
Trigger: Adjacent ally takes damage.
Effect: Use your reaction to apply Shield Block for your ally.
Tags:ReactionBlock

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Shoving-Stri.title: Ability - Shoving Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Shoving-Stri.content:
AP Cost: +1
When making a strike with an Impact or Unarmed weapon, you can declare a Shoving Strike. If you hit and deal damage, the target must roll Endure vs your attack roll or be Shoved — forcefully disengaged from the skirmish. Unlike the basic Shove, your attack roll uses any attribute your weapon allows.
Tags:Strike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Skirmisher's.title: Ability - Skirmisher's Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Skirmisher's.content:
AP Cost: -
After making a thrown attack within your weapon’s thrown range, leave your skirmish as a free Disengage. Once per turn.
Tags:RangedMovement

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Spell-Reflec.title: Ability - Spell Reflection
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Spell-Reflec.content:
AP Cost: R
When you critically succeed on a Deflect against a spell, you send it back towards the sender, making them roll defense against their own spell.
Tags:ReactionDeflect

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Spell-Shot.title: Ability - Spell Shot
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Spell-Shot.content:
AP Cost: Variable (spell cost)
When casting a single target offensive spell, you can store it in the knocked arrow until the end of your next turn, using your bow strike to resolve both the spells.

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Spend-Some-T.title: Ability - Spend Some Time with You
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Spend-Some-T.content:
AP Cost: weapon strike +2
Attempt a Feint or Shove check against an enemy in your skirmish. On success, you force them out: you and the target are removed from the skirmish into a duel — a new skirmish holding just the two of you — and you immediately strike, with the target Off-Guard against it. On failure, they resist and push you back: your momentum is broken, no strike happens, the AP is spent.
Tags:StrikeMovement

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Spinning-Sta.title: Ability - Spinning Staff
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Spinning-Sta.content:
AP Cost: 3
You spin your staff, turning it into a blur. Each enemy approaching you gets a strike as a free action until the start of your next turn or until the first successful deflection.
TBR - to be remade. Balance is off.
Tags:Strike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Storm-of-Arr.title: Ability - Storm of Arrows
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Storm-of-Arr.content:
AP Cost: TBD
Fire three rapid-draw shots, each at -2 to hit and -1 damage die. May distribute among targets in your skirmish or a connected zone.
Tags:AttackProjectile

Actions/Abilities/Ability---That-Type-of.title: Ability - That Type of a Person
Actions/Abilities/Ability---That-Type-of.content:
AP Cost: R
When an ally is downed in your zone, or in a zone you could reach by spending up to 2 AP on movement, move there as a free action and enter the skirmish in place of the incapacitated ally.
All checks - including defend - required to reach the destination are rolled with an advantage.
All offensive actions - including AOE - directed at the ally are directed at you instead. You can’t leave the ally until the end of combat or until the ally is no longer incapacitated.
Tags:ReactionMove

Actions/Abilities/Ability---The-Leader.title: Ability - The Leader
Actions/Abilities/Ability---The-Leader.content:
AP Cost: R
In the face of danger, you are the leader. When an enemy or an effect rolls to frighten you or your team, roll an opposed Leadership check. Your allies can choose between your roll and their roll of resistance. Two Leaders in one team will have both of their perks suppressed.
Tags:Reaction

Actions/Abilities/Ability---The-Wall.title: Ability - The Wall
Actions/Abilities/Ability---The-Wall.content:
AP Cost: R
Requirement: You carry a heavy shield.
Allies in your skirmish can hide behind you as a reaction, leaving the defense up to The Wall.
Tags:ReactionBlock

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Throw.title: Ability - Throw
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Throw.content:
AP Cost: 2
Requirement: You are grappling the target.
Release the grabbed target violently: deal your unarmed damage + Might, the target is forcefully disengaged from the skirmish and lands Prone.
Tags:StrikeBrawling

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Throwing-Dis.title: Ability - Throwing Distraction
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Throwing-Dis.content:
AP Cost: R
Trigger: An ally makes a strike, but didn’t roll yet.
Effect: Throw the weapon in your hand as a reaction. If you hit, you don’t deal damage, but the target becomes off-guard against the triggering attack.
Tags:ReactionRanged

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Too-Selfish.title: Ability - Too Selfish
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Too-Selfish.content:
AP Cost: -
Instant - This perk requires no training. When you stand your ground, but fail despite being a That Type of a Person, you can attempt to strike a bargain with the Master of The Universe.

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Tower-Defend.title: Ability - Tower Defender
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Tower-Defend.content:
AP Cost: All
Requirements: You have all AP you gained at the start of the turn.
Drop your quiver to the ground next to you. Each time an enemy enters a zone within your weapon’s range or enters your line of sight, make a basic ranged strike.
You can attack a number of times equal to your Tier. You cannot shoot the same target twice.
Tags:RangedStrike

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Tripping-Str.title: Ability - Tripping Strike
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Tripping-Str.content:
AP Cost: 3
Make a strike with the blunt part at enemy’s leg. If you succeed, enemy has to roll Dodge. On a failure, they fall prone.

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Two-Birds.title: Ability - Two Birds
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Two-Birds.content:
AP Cost: -1
Requirement: You are holding non-light melee weapon.
Make a melee strike 2 targets within skirmish. Resolve strikes one after another. Roll attack and damage once.
Tags:StrikeAoE

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Unarmed-Comb.title: Ability - Unarmed Combat
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Unarmed-Comb.content:
AP Cost: -
Your natural attacks no longer deal 1+Might damage. You gain two unarmed attacks:

Punch: d3 damage, Light, Nonlethal, 2 AP
Kick: d4 damage, Sweep, 3 AP

Actions/Abilities/Ability---Vanishing-St.title: Ability - Vanishing Step
Actions/Abilities/Ability---Vanishing-St.content:
AP Cost: R
Trigger: You successfully Dodge a melee attack.
Req: You are unencumbered,
Attempt a stealth check against your attacker’s perception with -5. On success you are Hidden.

Actions/Combat/Aim.title: Aim
Actions/Combat/Aim.content:
AP Cost: 1
Traits:Interact
Steady your aim before a ranged attack. Reduces the Distance DC of your next ranged attack by 2.
You can benefit from at most 2 Aims on a single attack (−4 Distance DC).

Actions/Combat/All-in-Defense.title: All in Defense
Actions/Combat/All-in-Defense.content:
AP Cost: 2
Traits:Defend
Requirement: You haven’t attacked this turn.
You enter a full defensive stance. AllDefend actions until the start of your next turn are rolled with an advantage. You can’t attack until the end of your turn.

Actions/Combat/Deflect.title: Deflect
Actions/Combat/Deflect.content:
AP Cost:
Traits:Defend
Roll: Martial + Agility/Dexterity/Might vs attack
Deflect a melee attack with your weapon or shield. The attribute used depends on weapon or shield type.

Actions/Combat/Disarm.title: Disarm
Actions/Combat/Disarm.content:
AP Cost: 2
Traits:Attack
Roll: Martial + Might/Dexterity vs the target’s weapon roll (2d10 + Martial + their weapon’s attack attribute)
Attempt to knock a weapon out of an opponent’s hands.

If the target is not Grabbed by you, you roll at -5, and on a failure the target may immediately make a basic attack against you as a free action.
If you have the target Grabbed, there is no penalty and failure carries no consequence.

On success, the weapon drops in your zone. Picking up a weapon is a 1 AP interaction.

Actions/Combat/Dodge.title: Dodge
Actions/Combat/Dodge.content:
AP Cost: -
Traits:Defend
Roll: Agility + Perception vs attack
Evade an incoming attack by moving out of the way.

Actions/Combat/Endure.title: Endure
Actions/Combat/Endure.content:
AP Cost: -
Traits:Defend
Roll: Endurance + Will vs effect
Resist physical ailments (poison, disease, exhaustion) or mental effects (fear, charm, mind control).

Actions/Combat/Escape.title: Escape
Actions/Combat/Escape.content:
AP Cost: 1
Traits:Attack
Roll: Choose one:

Unarmed or weapon strike vs grappler’s defense - AP as per strike’s AP cost
Athletics or Escape Artist vs DC 11 + grappler’s Brawling - 1 AP

Attempt to break free from the Effect - Grabbed condition. On success, lose the Grappled condition.

Actions/Combat/Feint-(WIP).title: Feint (WIP)
Actions/Combat/Feint-(WIP).content:
AP Cost: 1
Make a Feint: Martial + CH/DX vs target’s Resolve. On success, the target is Off-Guard against your next attack (one-time use).
Tags:Mind

Actions/Combat/Grapple.title: Grapple
Actions/Combat/Grapple.content:
AP Cost: 3
Traits:Attack
Requirements: One free hand
Roll: Martial + Might/Agility vs Dodge
Attempt to grab an opponent in your skirmish. On success, the target gains the Effect - Grabbed condition and you are locked together — neither of you can leave the skirmish while the grapple holds.
On failure, the defender may immediately make a basic attack against you as a free action.

Actions/Combat/Melee-Attack.title: Melee Attack
Actions/Combat/Melee-Attack.content:
AP Cost: 2-4 (based on weapon weight)
Traits:Attack
Roll: Martial + Attribute vs defense
Attack a target in the Skirmish.

Actions/Combat/Ranged-Attack.title: Ranged Attack
Actions/Combat/Ranged-Attack.content:
AP Cost: 2-4 (based on weapon weight)
Traits:AttackProjectile
Roll: Martial + Dexterity/Perception vs Distance DC, then vs defense
Attack a target at range with a ranged weapon. The attack must first beat the Distance DC based on range increment (see Ranged Combat), then the defender rolls Dodge — or Deflect, with a shield or perks — against your result (or other available defenses).

Actions/Combat/Ready.title: Ready
Actions/Combat/Ready.content:
Ready
AP Cost: Variable (activity AP cost)
Traits:Interact, +Traits of the prepared action
Prepare an action that will occur outside your turn.
Procedure

Spend the number of AP the readied activity requires
Declare a loose trigger condition (e.g., “when enemy enters reach,” “when ally is attacked,” “when door opens”)
End your turn immediately
When the trigger occurs, spend your Reaction to execute the readied activity

Observability
Most combat readying is obvious to observers - you’ve summoned a ball of fire and hold it in your hands, entered a striking stance, aimed your bow at the doorway, or positioned your spear defensively. GMs are advised to use common sense to manage metagaming. Hidden preparations require appropriate Stealth checks or concealment.
Examples

Ready a strike: Spend weapon AP, trigger “when enemy enters zone,” execute strike as Reaction
Ready a spell: Spend spell AP, trigger “when ally falls below half HP,” cast spell as Reaction
Ready movement: Spend movement AP, trigger “when enemy charges,” move as Reaction

Enhanced by: Various perks may reduce the AP cost of readying specific activities

Actions/Combat/Resolve.title: Resolve
Actions/Combat/Resolve.content:
AP Cost: -
Traits:Defend
Roll: Will + Charisma vs effect
Resist mental effects: fear, charm, mind control, and other assaults on the psyche.
Tags:Defense

Actions/Combat/Shove.title: Shove
Actions/Combat/Shove.content:
AP Cost: 3
Roll Martial + MG vs target’s Endure. On success, the target is Shoved — forcefully disengaged from its skirmish.
No damage, pure team tactics: kick the wizard out from behind his bodyguard — or the bodyguard away from his wizard — and jump the exposed target.
Tags:AttackMelee

Actions/Combat/Taunt.title: Taunt
Actions/Combat/Taunt.content:
AP Cost: 1
Traits:Social
Roll Manipulation against enemy’s Endure. You may specify your taunt and GM will give the enemy a penalty or a bonus against that roll.
On success enemy gets -1 to all attacking actions that don’t include you. On their next turn.

Actions/Combat/Trip.title: Trip
Actions/Combat/Trip.content:
AP Cost: 2
Traits:Attack
Roll: Martial + Might/Agility vs Endure
Attempt to knock an opponent in your skirmish to the ground. On success, the target gains the Condition - Prone condition.

Actions/Movement/Disengage.title: Disengage
Actions/Movement/Disengage.content:
AP Cost: 1
Traits:Move
Leave your current Skirmish safely.
You step out of melee and are no longer part of the skirmish. You stay in the same zone.
Leaving a skirmish any other way — moving out of the zone, being shoved or pulled, or any effect that takes you out of melee without a Disengage — can trigger enemy reactions and abilities (e.g. Reactive Strike).

Actions/Movement/Engage.title: Engage
Actions/Movement/Engage.content:
AP Cost: 1
Traits:Move
Join or start a Skirmish in your zone.
Pick a target in your zone and move into melee range with it. If the target is already in a skirmish, you engage everyone in that skirmish. If not, the two of you form a new one. You can engage an ally as well as an enemy — for example to shield them with your presence (see Strength in Numbers in Skirmish).
You can’t be in two skirmishes at once. If you are already in one, you have to leave it first — usually with Disengage.

Actions/Movement/Move.title: Move
Actions/Movement/Move.content:
AP Cost: Varies
Traits:Move
Move along a Line from your zone to a connected zone.
AP Cost = ceil((Line Distance × Multipliers from Effects) / Speed)
You must have the full cost available — there is no partial movement along a line. Some lines also require checks or impose hazards to cross; see Lines and Zones Effects.
If you are in a Skirmish, leaving the zone without a Disengage first can trigger enemy reactions.

Actions/Social/Ability---Comedian.title: Ability - Comedian
Actions/Social/Ability---Comedian.content:
AP Cost: R
Whenever words lead to a decrease in an attitude, roll Fast-Talk against GM set DC (based on the offense level) attempting to turn it into a joke. On a success the offense taken doesn’t decrease the attitude.
Tags:Reaction

Actions/Social/Deduce.title: Deduce
Actions/Social/Deduce.content:
Deduce
AP Cost: 1
Traits:Skill
Use knowledge skills for information through observation.

Actions/Social/Demoralize.title: Demoralize
Actions/Social/Demoralize.content:
Demoralize
AP Cost: 2
Traits:SkillBaneMind
Roll: Intimidation vs Endure

CLAUDE.title: CLAUDE
CLAUDE.content:
ExceedV TTXPG Core Rules Reference

Version Status: Milestone 6 (v0.6) in progress - Lines and Zones transition
See /MILESTONES.md for roadmap through v1.0

Game Overview

System: 2d10 dice system with advantage/disadvantage (3d10 keep 2)
Target Audience: Skill-based fantasy TTXPG for players wanting more control than class-based systems
Key Features:

Limit system prevents buff stacking
Skills and perks drive attributes (bottom-up design)
Armor as stamina multiplier
Bounded accuracy (skills/attributes capped at 5)



Core Resolution Mechanics
Dice System

Standard Roll: 2d10 + Skill + Attribute + Bonuses/Penalties
Advantage: 3d10 take 2
Disadvantage: 3d10 keep 2 lowest
Screwed: 1d10 (worst case - blinded, unconscious, severe curses)
Criticals: Doubles on kept dice (success → critical success, failure → critical failure)

Check Types

Unopposed: Roll result ≥ DC = Success
Opposed: Higher roll wins, doubles create critical success
Skill Applications:

Direct skill use: Full skill bonus
Raw attribute: Attribute only
Related skill: -1 to -3 penalty
Creative alternatives: GM discretion



Character Creation
Steps

Concept: Name and character concept
Starting XP: GM awards Combat XP and Skill XP separately
Spend XP: Skills, perks, spells (each shows which attributes benefit)
Calculate AP: Base 5 AP + Domain Tiers (Martial/Spellcraft)
Starting Gear: Equipment and final statistics

Attribute System

8 Core Attributes: Perception, Will, Charisma, Wit, Might, Endurance, Agility, Dexterity
Cannot buy directly: Only increase through skills/abilities
Threshold Progression: 10/30/60/100/150 points = +1 to attribute

Skill Progression

Regular Skills: 2/+4/+6/+8/+10 XP per level
Domains (Special Skills):

Spellcraft: 10/+20/+30/+40/+50 XP (progressed by learning spells)
Martial: 10/+20/+30/+40/+50 XP (progressed by learning perks and weapon training)



Weapon Training System (v0.5)

8 Weapon Categories: Brawling, Shield, Blades, Axes, Impact, Polearms, Bows, Thrown
Untrained Penalty: -2 to use weapons without training
Training Perks: 5 XP each, grants proficiency + category-specific bonus

Blades: Expanded crit range (beat defense by 10+ = crit)
Shield: Shield Block reaction (damage reduction on failed blocks)
Brawling: 2 AP and 3 AP unarmed attacks (supplementary)
Polearms: Ready strikes cost -1 AP (defensive stance)
Axes: Overswing (Reaction: +2 vs Deflect defense when declared, -2 to attackers defends till the start of next turn)
Thrown: Skirmisher’s Strike (Step back as part of thrown attack, once per turn)
Bows: Learn Aim action (works with all ranged weapons)
Impact: Shoving Strike (+1 AP, Impact or Unarmed; on hit target rolls Endure vs attack roll or is Shoved out of the skirmish)



Combat Perk Trees (v0.5)
Combat perks with 5+ interconnected requirements form perk trees organized into subfolders.
Perk Folder Structure (Perks/CombatPerks/):
Weapon Trees (Complete):

WeaponTraining/ - 8 weapon category training perks (Ax, Blades, Bow, Brawling, Impact, Polearms, Shield, Thrown)
Shields/ - Complete shield tree (9 perks: Shield Rush, Multipurpose Shield, Shield Warden, Perfect Block, Spell Guard, Shield Guardian, Behind the Shield Strike, The Wall, Guardian Aura)
Archery/ - Complete archery tree (15 files: Double Shot, Fast Archer, Tower, Hair Trigger, Mobile Draw, Tower Defender, Artillery, Spell Shot, Overpowered Draw, Close Quarters Shooter, Defensive Archer, Zen Archer, Don’t Turn Your Back On Me (Deprecated), WIP: Ricochet Shot, Storm of Arrows)
Footwork/ - Evasion and movement (9 perks: Footwork, Light Steps, Small Steps, Big Steps, Dodging Step, Elusive, Dodge-Roll, Dodge Behind Your Back, Come and Get Me)
Polearms/ - Polearm techniques (8 perks: Quarter-staff Adept, Walking Stick, Pointy Stick, Grip Switch, Spinning Staff, Monkey King Strike, Staff Acrobat, Spear Brothers)
Parrying And Riposte/ - Defensive counter-attacks (5 perks: Parry This Parry That, Painful Parry, Repose This Repose That, Riposte, Projectile Parry)
Dual Wielding/ - Two-weapon fighting (3 perks: Twin Parry, Double Strike, Ambidexterity)
Wrestling/ - Grappling tree (8 perks: Takedown, Drag Along, Wrestler’s Control, Iron Grip, Counter Grab, Weapon Thief, Chokehold, Throw)
Blades/ - Blade-specific techniques (3 perks: Ready Hand, Long Knives, The Edgelord)
Thrown/ - Thrown weapon techniques (2 perks: Throwing Hand, Throwing Distraction)

Other Categories:

Conditioning/ - HP progression perks (8 perks: Poison Resistance, Waterfall Training, Mental Resilience, Cold Conditioning, Heat Conditioning, Magical Conditioning, Battle Scarred, Bones of Steel)
Combat Maneuvers/ - Universal combat techniques (10 perks: Calf Strike, Tripping Strike, Piranha Strike, Mighty Charge, Follow-Up Strike, Two Birds, All the Birds; Duelist line: Spend Some Time with You, Just the Two of Us, You and I)
Shoving/ - Forced-movement strike line (4 perks: Herding Strike, Home Run, Bowling Strike, WIP Rocket Strike; builds on basic Shove action + Shoving Strike)
Predictive/ - Experimental predictive combat system (6 files: Predicted Exchange, Predictive Defense, Predictive Strike, Reactive Prediction, WIP Predict A Perfect Ambush, WIP Predicted Duel)

Social/Universal (Loose files and folders):

Leadership/ - Social leadership perks (4 perks: The Aspiring Hero, The Leader, The Cult Inner Member, The Cult Leader)
Backstab, Plot Armor, Reactive, Reactive Strike, That Type of a Person, The Loner, Too Selfish, Watching your back

Hit Points & Health
HP Pools

Stamina: (Armor + Endurance) × Max Wounds (depleted first)
Health: HP Per Wound × Max Wounds (+ bonuses from effects, e.g. Conditioning stages)
Starting: 2 Max Wounds, 5 HP Per Wound

Increasing HP

Extra HP Perk (v0.4, deprecated in v0.5): Max_Wounds × XP per level
Consolidation: Every 5 Extra HP levels → +1 Max Wound
v0.5 Replacement: Conditioning perks (same mechanics, thematic capstone rewards)

Poison Resistance, Waterfall Training, Mental Resilience, Cold/Heat Conditioning, Battle Scarred, Magical Conditioning



Combat System
Action Economy

Base: 5 AP + 1 Reaction per turn
Domain AP: Each Tier in Martial provides 1 AP usable withcombat abilities. Each Tier in Spellcraft provides 1 AP usable withspellcraft abilities.
Initiative: 2d10 + Perception
Surprise/Ambush: Coordinated initiative, stunned targets lose 3 AP

Defenses

Deflect: Martial + Agility/Dexterity/Might (based on weapon type) + Equipment Defense bonus
Dodge: Agility + Perception
Resolve: Will + Charisma
Endure: Endurance + Might

Combat Resolution Sequence (v0.6)

Attacker declares activity: “I swing at you”
Defender declares defense type: “I Deflect/Dodge/Resolve/Endure”
Attacker declares pre-roll boosts: Spending reactions, stances, abilities
Defender declares pre-roll boosts and reactions: Defensive abilities, buffs
Both roll
Resolve outcome

Movement System (v0.6)

Lines and Zones: Primary positioning system. Zones are abstract areas (rooms, squares, etc.). Lines connect zones with distance stats.
Skirmishes: Groups in melee range within a zone. Engage all targets in a skirmish with one action.
Numeric Advantage: -1 to deflect/dodge per disadvantage in skirmish (capped at -4). With at least 3 allies in your skirmish (or counting as having 3), no numeric disadvantage (back-to-back).
Reach Weapons: Attack without entering skirmish, count for numeric advantage.
Ranged Attacks: Range increment = ceil(Total Distance / Weapon Range). Same skirmish = point blank.

Defense Applications by Attack Type

Strike: Deflect, Dodge (melee, touch spells)
Projectile: Dodge, Deflect (with shield or perks)
Burst: Dodge (Deflect with perks)
Mind: Resolve (fear, charm, mind control)
Body: Endure (poison, disease, exhaustion)

Attacks & Damage

Weapon Stats: Agility for all, Heavy allows Might, Finesse allows Dexterity
Ranged: Dexterity or Perception based on weapon
Damage: Weapon Dice + Might + Bonuses
Damage Dice by Skill: 1-2 skill = 1 die, 3-4 skill = 2 dice, 5+ skill = 3 dice
Weapon AP Costs: Light = 2 AP, Normal = 3 AP, Heavy = 4 AP

Magic System
Core Principles

Mage Requirement: Must have Mage perk (GM permission)
Two Types: Passive (uses Limit) vs Active (requires casting roll)
Limit Stat: 3 + Will + Spellcraft (capacity for persistent effects)
Active Casting: 2d10 + Spellcraft + Wit vs DC [8 + Tier × 2]

Spellcraft Domain

Progression: Learning spells advances the domain
Tier Unlocks: Each Spellcraft level unlocks new spell tiers
Learning Requirements: Magical Theory/Theology ≥ spell tier (or teacher)
Learning Time: 1 day per XP spent

Spell Costs by Tier








































TierCostXP to Next Tier01-131025+2037+30410+40515+50

Note (v0.6): Advanced spell cost tier removed. Prerequisites now gate access — the Basic/Advanced split is no longer used. All spells cost a flat XP per tier.

Metamagic (v0.6)

Spell-modifying options granted bySpellcraftMetamagic perks (Perks/MagicPerks/Metamagic/); perk XP counts toward Spellcraft tiers like spells
Each application adds an AP surcharge and a casting DC surcharge (per-option); cap = Spellcraft tier per cast
Attuned spells pay +1 Limit per application instead of DC
Grand Weaving (Spellcraft 3) removes the cap and allows multi-turn casting
Options: Reaching, Subtle, Lingering, Split, Widened, Empowered + Grand Weaving
Specializations (bonus inside/penalty outside): Mage of an Element, Inward Focus, Withering Focus

Skills List
Social Skills

Dancing (Agility/Charisma), Negotiating (Charisma/Wit), Manipulation (Charisma/Will)
Leadership (Charisma/Will), Fast-talk (Charisma/Agility), Singing (Endurance/Charisma)
Gossip (Charisma/Perception), Intimidation (Charisma/Might), Acting (Charisma/Will)

Athletic Skills

Running (Agility/Endurance), Climbing (Might/Agility), Swimming (Endurance/Might)
Jumping (Might/Agility), Acrobatics (Agility/Dexterity), Lifting (Might/Endurance)
Breaking (Might/Wit)

Knowledge Skills

Magical Theory (Wit/Will), History (Wit/Will), Theology (Will/Charisma), Streetwise (Charisma/Perception)

Other Categories

Crafting: Smithing, Woodworking, Textilework, Engineering
Sciences: Biology, Chemistry, Medicine
Stealth/Criminal: Stealth, Lockpicking, Sleight of Hand
Wilderness: Survival, Tracking, Navigation

Traits System
Defense Traits

Strike: Deflect, Dodge
Projectile: Dodge, Deflect (with shield or perks)
Burst: Dodge (Deflect with perks)
Mind: Resolve
Body: Endure
Defend: Generic trait for all defensive actions (Deflect, Dodge, Resolve, Endure) - used for buffs like “All in Defense”

Effect Types

Boon: Beneficial effects
Bane: Detrimental effects
Protection: Damage mitigation
Healing: Health restoration

Bonus Types (Stacking Rules)

Same type: Don’t stack, take higher
Different types: Stack together
Types:Competence,Morale,Enhancement,Luck,Equipment,Situational,Armor,Size
Condition stacking: Same condition = highest applies, opposites negate, different types stack
Condition range: +3 to -3

Conditions System
Conditions are stored in /source/content/Rules/References/Conditions/ and defined in 4.3 Conditions.md
Duration Presets

One-Time Use - Next qualifying action (luck effects, feint Off-Guard)
End of Turn - Fades at turn end (Shaken, Flash Blinded)
Until Removed - Source specifies removal (Grabbed, Off-Guard while prone, Dazzled until cleared)

Enhancement Conditions (Attribute Modifiers)

Grace X: ±X to Agility/Dexterity rolls
Vigor X: ±X to Might/Endurance rolls
Focus X: ±X to Willpower/Perception rolls
Sharpness X: ±X to Charisma/Wit rolls
Quickened X: ±X actions at start of turn

Morale Conditions

Shaken X: X morale penalty on all rolls
Inspired X: X morale bonus on all rolls

Luck Conditions

Jinxed: Next roll at disadvantage
Blessed: Next roll at advantage

Situational Conditions

Prone: Disadvantage on Martial Domain (attacks, Deflect). Advantage on Dodge/Resolve/Endure vsProjectile andBurst. Movement speed reduced to 1.
Grabbed: -2 to attacking/manipulating, intricate actions at disadvantage, no reach weapons vs grappler. Grappler releases free; grappled must Escape.
Off-Guard: -1 to defend against attacks.
Blinded: All sight-reliant checks are Screwed (1d10).
Dazzled: All sight-reliant checks at disadvantage.
Unconscious: Deflect/Dodge are Screwed, Perception at disadvantage.

Rest Conditions

Fatigued X: -X to all rolls, -2X to exploration/downtime. At Fatigue 4, unconscious.
Well Rested: +1 to +3 to Downtime/Exploration until Fatigued or night’s rest.

Damage Riders (no ticking DOTs — temp design v0.6)

No damage-over-time; lingering harm = front-loaded damage, one-time riders, or zone hazards (track the map, not tokens)
Bleed X: next movement action → take X, then clears (First Aid clears safely)
Fragile X: next damage instance +X, then clears
Pinned X: next movement action +X AP, or 1 AP to remove projectile
Stunned X (defined): Lose X AP at start of turn, no reactions until next turn; excess carries over

Social Interactions
Attitude System

Range: -5 (hostile) to +5 (fanatical adoration)
Factors: Race, appearance, social class, rank
Favor Costs: Attitude affects price (negative = higher cost, positive = lower/free)

Social Actions

Affect Attitude: Social skill + Charisma vs target’s resistance
Detect Falsehood: Perception + Manipulation or Perception + Will
Fast-Talk: Fast-talk vs Detect Falsehood or Perception/Will

Trading

Base Prices: Pawn shops buy 50%, sell 100% of listed price
Attitude Modifier: ±5% per attitude step
Bargaining Range: 25-125% of listed price based on attitude

Key Actions
Movement

Engage: 1 AP - Enter a skirmish within a zone
Disengage: 1 AP - Leave a skirmish without provoking reactions
Move: Variable AP - Move between zones (Cost = ceil((Distance × Multiplier) / Speed)), no partial movement
Stand Up: 2 AP - Remove Prone condition

Combat Actions

Basic Attack: 2-4 AP based on weapon weight
All in Defense: 2 AP - Gain advantage on allDefend actions until your next turn (requires no offensive action this turn)
Grapple: 3 AP - Attempt to grab opponent (Brawling + Might/Agility vs defense). On success, both gain Grabbed condition.
Escape: 1 AP - Attempt to break free from Grabbed condition (Athletics or Escape Artist vs grappler’s Brawling)
Disarm: 2 AP - Martial + MG/DX vs target’s weapon roll; -5 and free retaliation on failure unless target is Grabbed by you
Trip: 2 AP - Martial + MG/AG vs Endure; target Prone
Shove: 3 AP - Martial + MG vs Endure; target forced out of its skirmish (no damage, team tactic)
Feint (WIP): 1 AP - Martial + CH/DX vs Resolve; target Off-Guard vs your next attack
Ready (v0.5): Variable AP (activity cost) - prepare action with trigger, execute as Reaction

Examples: Ready strike, ready spell, ready movement
Most combat preparations are obvious to observers


First Aid: 4 AP, Medicine skill
Aid: 2+R AP, provides bonus to ally

Social Actions

Demoralize: 1 AP, Intimidation vs Endure
Deduce: 1 AP, knowledge skills for information

Design Philosophy

Bounded Accuracy: Skills/attributes max at 5
Positive Feedback: Higher skills → higher attributes → better performance
Player Agency: Choose attribute increases when raising skills
Resource Management: Limit system for magical effects
Tactical Depth: Multiple defense options and action economy choices

Ability & Effect System (GAS-Inspired)
Naming Convention
The system uses Unreal Engine GAS (Gameplay Ability System) naming conventions:

Abilities: Active actions players choose to use (files prefixed with Ability - )
Effects: Passive bonuses, triggers, or ongoing modifications (files prefixed with Effect - )

File Structure
/source/content/Actions/Abilities/Ability - Name.md    → Contains ability mechanics only
/source/content/Rules/Effects/Effect - Name.md         → Contains effect mechanics only
/source/content/Perks/Category/Perk Name.md    → Contains XP cost, requirements, embeds ability/effect

Ability vs Effect Decision Tree

Is it an active choice the player makes? → Ability

Examples: Strike attacks, reactions, castable spells, preparing actions


Is it always on or triggers automatically? → Effect

Examples: Stat bonuses, expanded crit ranges, passive auras, conditional triggers



File Format
Ability Files (Ability - Name.md):
Description of what the ability does and how it works.
 
**Tags:** #RelevantTags #ForMechanics

**Requirements:** Prerequisites
**Attributes:** Affected attributes
**Cost:** XP cost

No Duplication: Ability/effect mechanics live in one file only

Parser-Friendly: Files identifiable by Ability -  or Effect -  prefix

Creating New Abilities/Effects

Write mechanics (no “Ability:” or “Effect:” label needed - filename shows type)

Design Decisions & Logic
Unique Selling Proposition (USP)
The Limit System - The core innovation of Exceed is the “Limit” stat, which governs the maximum number of persistent magical and non-magical effects a character can sustain simultaneously.
Problem Solved
Traditional systems suffer from “pre-buff” issues where players stack numerous temporary bonuses before encounters, and “magic item bloat” where characters accumulate dozens of persistent magical effects. D&D 5e attempts to address this with concentration, time limits, and attunement slots, while PF2E uses 10 attunement slots but still allows hundreds of different buffs to stack.
Solution: Limit
The Limit stat creates a hard cap on the total number of active persistent effects, forcing meaningful tactical choices:

Players must prioritize which effects to maintain
No endless stacking of buffs
Clear, trackable resource management
Scales with character power (Limit increases as characters advance)
Applies to all persistent effects: spells, permanent magic items, class abilities, etc.

This system eliminates bookkeeping nightmares while maintaining strategic depth through meaningful choice constraints.
Core Concepts
The game aims to fix 3 problems recurrent in TTRPGs

Buff Stacking/Endless Buffing, character progression disconnected from the play-style, and armor-hp interactions.
For this it offers its USPs as solutions.
The Limit system in 6. Magic System - limiting the active buffs and magical effects a character can sustain on self and group.

3.3 HP And Wounds. - where Armor works as ablation multiplied by the character’s resilience.
2. 3.1 Attributes - Attributes deriving from skills, creating positive feedback loops, separation of social and combat XP based on the session contents.
Target Audience
Skill-based TTRPG enjoyers. Earned progression connoisseurs.
Target audience is TTRPG players who prefer when they are not dictated how to play a character from the moment they choose the class at level 1.
It still absolutely should work for new players as well as experienced ones. Though groups with new players are suggested lower XP starting point.
It’s a game for GURPS players who want less complexity and more streamlined experience, Pathfinder players who want more control over their characters, LitRPG lovers who love numbers go up, slow burn progression.

Rules/Combat/4.0-Lines-and-Zones.title: 4.0 Lines and Zones
Rules/Combat/4.0-Lines-and-Zones.content:
The maps in Exceed are defined in Lines and Zones. Maps can be used with or without a grid, as distances are tracked with lines — no map at all, or a map on a napkin, works as well as any other map.
A creature’s position amounts to two things: its whereabouts (what Zone it is in), and who it’s contending or shielding with in melee (its Skirmish).
Zones
Zones are abstract areas — a room, an alleyway, a hilltop, a city square. The GM decides the zoning based on the needs of the scene.
Within a zone, you can get into a Skirmish with an enemy or an ally with a single Engage action, followed by an attack or other offensive ability.
When you Engage an enemy or an ally — or they engage you — you engage all the targets in that Skirmish.
Transclude of Skirmish
Lines
Lines represent the distance between zones. Each line has a Distance statistic and can hold effects.
Line of sight: blocking line of sight is a property of a line (a wall, a corner, thick smoke). Generally, whether a zone can be seen from another is up to the GM.
Cost of traversal = Distance × Multipliers from Effects
AP to Move = ceil(Cost / Speed)
You must have the full AP cost available to cross — there is no partial movement along a line. GMs are advised to write the costs on the map next to each line to keep track of the effects.
! Rule of thumb
Lines should cost no more than 20 in the late game and no more than 10 in the early game. When designing a map, no zone should be further than about 2/3 of a turn of Move from its neighbors on average.
To calculate distance between disconnected zones reference Distance in Combat.
Effects
Lines and Zones can hold effects that modify the rules — providing effects, abilities and alike.
Environmental, situational or magical — some can be removed, suppressed or bypassed by abilities explicitly stating so, or with checks and improvisation approved by the GM.
Examples:
Line is a wall, requiring DC 15 climbing check and distance 10.
“Hey GM, I want to cast levitate on the group” / “Hey GM, I want to be a big guy and help others climb by jump-starting them” / “Hey GM, can I throw my rope dart and climb that way”
“Cast the spell / Lower the DC by 5 if you spend your whole turn on this / Add an extra AP, and reduce DC by 3.”
Defaults on Effects in Lines and Zones Effects.

Rules/Combat/4.1-Taking-Damage.title: 4.1 Taking Damage
Rules/Combat/4.1-Taking-Damage.content:
Players take damage as per Health and Wounds first depleting stamina, then depleting health. Players can reach negative HP with a value of Max Health not accounted for wounds.
Getting Below 0 HP and Death
Getting to 0 Health: Each time your Health reaches or goes below 0, roll a Consequence Roll , and mark 1 wound.
When at or below 0 Health you need to roll Endure vs Treatment DC of your highest treatment DC wound to stay conscious at the start of each of your turns.

Each lethal hit you take in this state makes you roll a Consequence Roll.
Each non-lethal hit you take in this state makes you roll Endure against the hit to stay conscious.

When below negative full Health - you fall unconscious without a check. Unless the attack was nonlethal you also need to roll Endure vs Treatment DC to stay alive at the end of each of your turns.
Death: If your lethal wounds would exceed max wounds or reach negative HP due to a lethal attack, you die. If your overall wounds (including non-lethal) exceed your max wounds you go unconcious.

Conditions in Exceed apply bonuses, penalties and ongoing effects.

All types of conditions range from max +3 to min -3.
Most conditions use the default 3 duration presets from the effects and abilities that apply them. This is written in natural language, but follows these basic presets.
1. One-Time Use (next qualifying action)

Advantage/Disadvantage from luck, or pre-rolls fromprediction abilities.
Off-Guard from feint.
2. End of Turn (fades at turn end)
Shaken from Demoralize
Blinded from Flash
3. Until Removed (The source should specify removal conditions)

Grabbed while grapple maintained (removed by grappler’s release or Escape action)
Dazzled until clears eyes with a DC 10 DX check.
Shaken 2 while in Fear Aura. (leaving aura)
Focus -2 from a combat maneuver requiring a first aid or a breather.

Conditions are to be revamped in MS6.
1. Enhancement Conditions

Grace X: +-X to Agility (AG) and Dexterity (DX) based rolls.
Vigor X: +-X to Might (MG) and Endurance (EN) based rolls.
Focus X: +-X to Willpower (WL) and Perception (PR) based rolls.
Sharpness X: +-X to Charisma (CH) and Wit (WT) based rolls.
Quickened X:  +-X actions at the start of each turn.

2. Rest related conditions
Transclude of Well-Rested
Transclude of Condition---Fatigued
3. Morale Conditions
This penalty affects a character’s ability to perform certain types of actions, representing fear, doubt, or a lack of confidence.

Shaken X: X morale penalty on all rolls.
Inspired X: X morale bonus on all rolls.

3. Luck

Jinxed - next roll of a specific type or simply the next roll is rolled with disadvantage.
Blessed - next roll of a specific type or simply the next roll is rolled with an advantage.

Transclude of Condition---Prone

5. Damage Riders — Musings (temp design, no DOTs)
Exceed does not use ticking damage-over-time. Most combats last about 3 rounds — a DOT that ticks twice is just damage with bookkeeping. Lingering harm takes one of these forms instead:

Front-loaded damage — deal it now.
One-time riders — conditions that trigger once on the target’s next qualifying event, then clear (duration preset 1):

Bleed X: the next time the target spends AP on a movement action (Engage, Disengage, Move, Stand Up), it takes X damage, then Bleed clears. First Aid clears it without harm.
Fragile X: the next instance of damage the target takes deals +X, then Fragile clears. (cracked armor, opened guard)
Pinned X: (arrows, spears) the target’s next movement action costs +X AP, or it spends 1 AP to remove the projectile. Then clears.


Map effects — persistent harm lives on the map, not on tokens: set the zone on fire, fill it with poison gas (Hazardous zone — damage or an Endure roll at the start of a turn spent in it). The GM tracks one zone, not five creatures. This is also the long-fight answer: don’t DOT the boss — set his throne room on fire.
Out of combat — poisons, disease and untreated wounds run through Fatigue and the Consequences system, not combat conditions.

Same condition applied twice: keep the highest X, refresh the trigger.

Rules/Combat/4.4-Weapons-and-Combat-Trai.title: 4.4 Weapons and Combat Training
Rules/Combat/4.4-Weapons-and-Combat-Trai.content:
Combat skill in Exceed is determined by one’s Martial Domain.
To advance in the Combat Domain, you must learn combat perks. Weapon-specific combat perks require Weapon Training - proficiency in a weapon category gained through training perks with theWeaponTraining trait.
Weapon Categories:

Brawling - Fists, kicks, grappling
Shield - All shields
Blades - Knives, swords, daggers, sabres (slashing/piercing edged weapons)
Ax - Axes, picks, cleavers (chopping weapons)
Impact - Clubs, hammers, maces, flails (bludgeoning weapons)
Polearms - Spears, staves, halberds, pikes, glaives (long reach weapons)
Bows - Bows, crossbows (string-drawn ranged)
Thrown - Darts, javelins, throwing axes, slings (hand-propelled ranged)

Weapon Training Perks: Each weapon category has a corresponding training perk that costs 5 XP. These perks grant basic proficiency (removing the -2 untrained penalty) and provide a unique tactical ability specific to that weapon category.
Untrained Penalty: Using a weapon without training in its category imposes a -2 competence penalty to all rolls.

Martial advances through XP spent on combat perks (including weapon training). All such XP accumulates toward the tier thresholds — the domain is never bought directly:

Rules/Core/3.2-Perks-and-Flaws.content:
What Are Perks?
Perks represent specific training, experiences, conditions or specializations your character has undergone. They embody the “how” and “why” behind your character’s capabilities.
Perks cost XP and represent investments in specific areas of expertise. When you take a perk, you typically gain attribute points equal to the XP spent (some perks are free and some are without an attribute). These attribute points bring selected attributes closer to their next threshold (positive or negative).
Most perks don’t have levels, but some do. In that case each previous level overrides each next level, as per perk description.
Example of overriding are:
Conditioning perks - Conditioning Perks Overview
Perks may have prerequisites (other perks, skills, or attributes) and provide mechanical benefits that reflect your character’s specialized training.
Perk Categories

Combat Perks: Specialized combat techniques, weapon training, tactical abilities
Skill Perks: Specialized applications of skills (though skill perks don’t directly increase skill levels)
Spellcraft Perks: Magical specializations and techniques

How Perks Work

Spend Combat XP or Skill XP to purchase a perk
Choose which attribute receive the XP points (following the perk’s specifications, if any)
The XP spent becomes attribute points that move the chosen attribute toward the next threshold
Example: Spend 5 XP on a combat perk, choose Might → Might gains 5 points toward +1 threshold

Perks follow the ability/effect system structure where abilities are active choices and effects are passive bonuses.

Knowledge Skills
1. Magical Theory (Wit/Will) - Magic theory, spell identification, understanding magical phenomena
2. History (Wit/Will) - Past events, cultures, legends, political knowledge
3. Theology (Will/Charisma) - Divine knowledge, rituals, religious traditions
4. Streetwise (Charisma/Perception) - Criminal underworld knowledge, black market connections

Rules/Design-Philosophy.title: Design Philosophy
Rules/Design-Philosophy.content:
Exceed TTRPG - Design Philosophy
Game design documentation, not a final rulebook. Includes design reasoning and decision rationale.

Core Game Concepts
What Makes Exceed Different

Limit System - Prevents endless buff stacking by limiting active magical effects
Armor as Stamina Multiplier - Armor provides ablation based on character resilience
Skills Drive Attributes - Attributes derive from skills, creating positive feedback loops

Target Audience

GURPS players wanting less complexity
Pathfinder and DnD players wanting more character control
Players who prefer earned progression over class-based advancement
Groups who enjoy slow-burn character development


Key Design Logic

Bounded Accuracy: Skills and attributes capped at 5 for predictable math and balanced progression
Positive Feedback Loop: Higher skills → higher attributes → better performance with related skills
Player Agency: Players choose which attribute to increase when raising skills
GM Flexibility: GM determines appropriate skill/attribute combinations and situational penalties


Attribute System Philosophy
Bottom-Up Skill-Driven Design

Cannot directly buy attributes - only skills and abilities that grant attribute points
Skills increase related attributes as secondary benefits
This creates natural relationships between the 8 core attributes without explicit hierarchy

Design Decision
Removed the hierarchical attribute structure (Body/Mind → 4 main → 8 sub) as it created unnecessary complexity with the bottom-up system. Skills naturally create relationships between the 8 core attributes without needing to show the implicit 2→4→8 structure (2 cores: body and mind, each having control and raw power, split into usage methods).

Version Notes

Current Status: v0.4 → v0.5 WIP

Martial domain restructure in progress
Weapon training system implementation ongoing
Combat perk overhaul planned
Extra HP deprecation (replacing with Conditioning perks)

Rules/Downtime-And-Exploration/9.1-Time-.title: 9.1 Time and Travel
Rules/Downtime-And-Exploration/9.1-Time-.content:
Exceed  Time
Time in Exceed is measured using a power of 10 system starting with heartbeats and ending with days.
Time units are:




























































UnitDurationReference and termsHearbeatLess then a secondBeat, instantRound10 Hearbeats9s, a short momentMinuta10 Rounds90s, a short taskBreather10 Minutas15m, Quick restShift10 BreathersA work/study shiftsDay10 ShiftsFrom dawn to nextTenday10 Days2 ‘work weeks’Season10 Tendays(100d)1/3 of a yearWhen abilities mention time  change by magnitude - move the unit up or down by the magnitude. E.g. wound that needs a season to recover with aid will recover in a Tenday.In the world of Exceed, towns usually have full-day clocks that ring bells every half a shift after dawn, and workplaces have shift clocks, with the last section of a shift being a usual breather time.
Full night’s rest requires 3 Shifts.
Travel Speed
Travel Speed
Each character has a Travel Speed, equal to their Speed –Exploration activities for that Shift.
Use the lowest Travel Speed in the party when calculating group travel.
Apply Route Difficulty as follows:

Open Route: Travel Speed × 3 km
Moderate Route: Travel Speed × 2 km
Strenuous Route: Travel Speed × 1 km
Very Strenuous Route: Cannot be traveled without first reducing its difficulty.


Reducing Route Difficulty
Some abilities, skills, and spells can help you overcome harsh routes.
Effects from the same source (such as a single spell, perk, or exploration activity) stack, while different sources do not, allowing you to reduce the route penalty multiple times when using related effects.

Marching and Fatigue
You can make up to three Marches per day without a check.
Each additional March beyond the third requires a DC 10 Endure or Running check.

Increase the DC by +5 for each consecutive extra March that day.
On failure, you gain the Fatigued condition.
You cannot Force March while Fatigued.


Forced March
A Forced March doubles your travel distance for one March (×2) but counts as two Marches toward your daily limit.
During this, no character can perform more than one Exploration activity.
If you fail the fatigue check, the Forced March becomes a normal March, and you gain the Fatigued condition at the end of it.

Example
If you march three times and then continue, the check DC is 10.
If you choose to Force March instead, the DC is 15.
Earth time Variant rule
Time in Exceed can be counted as normal, with rounds, minutes, hours, and weeks. But is intended to be used with Exceed’s time system.
In Some abilities might mention that they lower or increase the required time spent by a magnitude or multiplication.
When multiplying, we use normal multiplication rules, and when changing magnitude, the magnitude steps are.
||1 Round|
|2|1 Minute|
|3|10 Minutes|
|4|1 Hour|
|5|1 Day|
|6|1 Week|
|7|1 Month|
|8|1 Year|
with a 10 multiplier after that.
travel earth time
Using Earh time count 1km per speed, half for difficult terrain, and quarter for greater. All rounded down.

Rules/Downtime-And-Exploration/9.3-Explo.content:
Circumvent Security Device
Traits: —
This activity allows a character to disarm traps, pick locks, bypass wards, or overcome similar security devices.
Each device defines:

Successes required
Time per attempt
Applicable skills
Consequences of failure


How It Works
When attempting to circumvent a device, roll the relevant skill once per attempt.
Each success counts toward the total number required.
Unless stated otherwise:

A failure wastes the time spent.
A critical failure escalates the situation at the GM’s discretion (jammed lock, triggered trap, etc.).


Examples
Average Lock

Successes Required: 1
Time per Attempt: 1 Minuta
Skills: Lock-picking, Breaking
Consequence: None — the attempt simply fails.


Alarming Ward

Successes Required: 2
Time per Attempt: 1 Breather
Skills: Magical Theory; Lock-picking (–2 penalty)
Consequence: On failure, the magical alarm triggers.


High-End Wall Safe

Successes Required: 3
Time per Attempt: 1 Shift
Skills: Lock-picking, Breaking
Consequence:

On failure, the lock jams, increasing the total successes required by +1 (maximum 5).
On critical failure, the safe becomes jammed, requiring at least a 4 shifts worth of repair.



Forage
Traits:Exploration , Speed Penalty 1.
You try to gather food, herbs or materials.
The DC is static based on the nature of the place and availability of resources. Skill is dependent on the environment and the target of foraging, usually being Biology for herbs, survival for food and water and burning materials in wilderness, streetwise for in city environments.
Each attempt at Foraging takes one Shift.
You can forage on the go, during marching, camping etc by lowering your speed by 1 and increases the DC by 2.
Number of rations/materials foraged are loosely rules by the GM.
Critical effects
On a critical success you find double the amount or something extra up to GM.
On a critical failure you encounter possible trouble - misidentify the food, get predator’s attention, or similar.
Examples for Game Masters
Lush forest


DC to forage food is 10. Herbs is 12. Materials is Up to GM.


Food foraging will provide 3 rations on success.


Herbs will provide 3 batches.
Hillside


DC to forage  food is 12. Herbs is 14. Materials is Up to GM.


Food foraging will provide 2 rations on success.


Herbs will provide 2 batches.
Mountain


DC to forage  food is 14. Herbs is 16. Materials is Up to GM.


Food foraging will provide 2 rations on success.


Herbs will provide 2 batches.
Deserted area


DC to forage  food is 16. Herbs is 20. Materials is Up to GM.


Food foraging will provide 1 rations on success.


Herbs will provide 1 batches.


Scouting
Traits:Exploration , Speed Penalty 2.SecretRoll
You move a bit ahead of the group and check the perimeter while remaining hidden.
The DC is based on the Stealth DC of the Enemy ambush, if there is one, or the Perception of the creatures ahead. If the creatures ahead are not hiding or on guard, you automatically succeed on the check.
Tracking
Traits:Exploration,SecretRoll   Speed Penalty - Varies.
You follow signs of passage — footprints, broken branches, scents, or magical traces — to locate creatures or groups. The DC is determined by the GM depending on environmental and target details.
GM decides attempt duration from minutas to days. This will be
Speed Penalty

Untrained or using another skill (e.g. Survival): –2 Speed
Tracking Skill 1–2: –1 Speed
Tracking Skill 3+: No Speed penalty

Success and Failure

Success: You follow the tracks successfully.
Failure: You lose the trail and waste the time spent.
Critical Success: You gain additional insight (direction, speed, number, or proximity) or reduce travel time.
Critical Failure: You follow false tracks and must return to the last confirmed location before resuming.

Rules/Intro/1.-Welcome-to-Exceed.title: 1. Welcome to Exceed
Rules/Intro/1.-Welcome-to-Exceed.content:
Exceed is a skill-based fantasy tabletop role-playing game using polyhedral dice.
The Game Master, like in most TTRPGs sets the scenes, and represents the characters who are not the players (NPCs), the monsters, and the world as a whole.
Game is designed to be played in group of three to six players, but should work with 1-2 players as well.
Core Philosophy of the game can be best observed in how it handles Character Development, Magic and many other mechanics in the game.
e.g.
Bottom-Up Character Development: Instead of saying “You’re strong, so you’re good at athletics,” Exceed asks “Why are you strong?”, instead of saying “You are good with combat so your good with swinging.” it asks “What maneuvers and training made you good?“.
Character growth follows logical story progression: training something narrow makes you better at adjacent things and builds pockets of specialization that allow you to exceed the narrow confines of many other systems. A skilled swordsman won’t be utterly useless given another weapon, unless you want him to, of course.
The game emphasizes player agency, tactical depth, and character development connected to the character progression. Rather than starting with predetermined classes putting you on a rails, the characters grow organically during the games through learning perks, getting flaws and rising through organizations to something you were not expecting them to be.
Flow
Game is played in sessions, and is designer to work for campaigns spreading multiple sessions, and isn’t well designed for one-shot adventures due to the crunchy nature of its systems.
It requires some background calculations to remove the tracking that comes with the system, that is why, using an application or VTT (when that will be available in the future) is advised.
Tools
The game doesn’t provide printed rules and character sheets, using digital ones instead, currently publicly hosted online. Thus a device is required.
For a in-person game a set of dice including two ten sided dice are required, preferably for each player, but dice rollers are fine as well.
For combat it is preferred to have miniatures, but theater of mind and vtt are or will be viable as well.
In future iterations, distance might be counted using a ruler as main distance calculation option, but that is up to playtesting.
Game for a few
In Exceed we believe in gate-keeping the fun, because when something belongs to everyone - it belongs to no one. This game belongs to me.
This game allows diversity of builds and play-styles, it does not engage in modern identity-based themes and contemporary social commentary neither in its mechanics, nor in the narratives.
When it does - it follows the classical narratives and eschews post-modern ones. It is obvious from its game design, but I am just spelling it out.
If you feel uncomfortable - leave, there are games for Everyone out there. This isn’t one.
Ready to play?
Get your phones/tablets/laptops/PCs out and proceed to the Basic rules. Go through them in an ordered manner.

Rules/Lines-And-Zones/Skirmish.title: Skirmish

A group in a zone that are in melee range with each other. A single character can’t be in 2 engagements at the same time.
Strength in numbers
Unless a zone states otherwise having a numerical disadvantage within a skirmish provides -1 to deflect and dodge rolls per difference to the defender capped at -4. The cap applies to the numeric-advantage penalty only — other penalties (e.g. Off-Guard) stack beyond it.
Back-to-back: if you have at least 3 allies in your skirmish (or count as having 3 allies), you no longer suffer the numeric disadvantage on defense.
Example: 2 guards skirmish 5 bandits — each guard deflects and dodges at -3 (outnumbered 5 to 2). Two more guards join: each of the 4 guards now has 3 allies in the skirmish, so back-to-back applies and they defend with no numeric penalty despite still being outnumbered.
Reach and Range weapons allow attacking without entering the skirmish, the attacks count the attacker for the benefit of numeric advantage for that attack.
To disengage from the Skirmish you need to perform a Disengage action. Trying to Leave the Skirmish with or without a Disengage action can interact with an ability of an effect.
